alalal-c42513-d1e101.summary: Rubric marking the division of Lombard's text for Distinction 37.

alalal-c42513-d1e108.summary: Identifies the subject of this part of Lombard's text ('Et quoniam demonstratum est'): how God is in creatures as cause in effect, by essence, presence and power.
claims: God is in creatures as cause in effect, essentially, presentially and potentially.

alalal-c42513-d1e127.summary: Divides the part in two. First Lombard shows that God is everywhere and in every thing. Since being in place implies moving through place, and being in a thing implies changing with it, he then shows that God remains immutable when place or thing changes ('Cumque divina natura veraciter').
claims: God's presence in every place and thing does not make him subject to local motion or change.

alalal-c42513-d1e156.summary: Divides the first part into three: Lombard determines and explains the modes of God's being everywhere; raises questions that follow ('Si autem quaeris, ubi habitabat Deus'); and returns to the first mode according to an opinion that spoke truly but insufficiently ('Ex praedictis patet').

alalal-c42513-d1e191.summary: Divides the first subpart into four chapters: a simple statement of the modes of God's being in things; proof by authority that God is in all things by essence, presence and power; proof that he dwells specially in the saints; and a reference back to the mission of the Holy Spirit for the mode of this indwelling.
claims: God dwells specially in the saints, beyond his general presence in all things.

alalal-c42513-d1e220.summary: Closing remark: the sense of the first part is clear from the division.

alalal-c42513.summary: Division of Lombard's text for the first part of Distinction 37, on how God is in creatures as cause in effect by essence, presence and power. Lombard first shows that God is everywhere and in every thing, and then that he remains immutable when the places and things he is in change. The first part has three sections: the modes of omnipresence, including God's special indwelling in the saints, which is referred back to the doctrine of the Holy Spirit's mission; questions that follow from this; and a return to the first mode as an earlier opinion stated it, truly but insufficiently.
claims: God is in creatures as cause in effect, by essence, presence and power.
God is specially present in the saints by indwelling.
God's presence everywhere does not make him mutable or locally movable.
